AI_never_authorization_authority.reason: No AI component participates in device registration, listing, revocation, or trust reporting (no ai/ import in devices/*, deviceClient.ts, deviceRuntimeState.ts).

client_never_final_authorization_authori.reason: Device trust as consumed by the desktop is asserted by the renderer over a PUBLIC IPC channel (contracts.ts:136-139; runtimeAuthz.ts:1053); device identity is client-minted with no proof (liveSyncInstance.ts:84). Registry MUTATION authority (revoke/remove) correctly sits on the backend role check (service.ts:82-88) — that part holds.

network_connection_must_not_imply_author.reason: Desktop requireCloudOrgMembership fails closed when the backend is unreachable (runtimeCore.ts:392-410; tested). But a valid JWT + active membership grants every device-scoped and sync action irrespective of device trust, so the device layer adds no authorization signal at all.

stale_authorization_must_be_rejected.reason: deviceRuntimeState is set once per Settings-pane visit and never expires, refreshes, or clears on sign-out (deviceRuntimeState.ts:18-27; single writer runtimeCore.ts:2374). A 'trusted' report outlives a backend revocation for the process lifetime; the backend itself never re-evaluates trust on any request.

control_compute_evidence_verification_hu.reason: HUMAN (owner/admin) -> CONTROL (revoke row) exists; COMPUTE never reads the control state; EVIDENCE limited to a health badge; no VERIFICATION that a revoked device stopped; no HUMAN DECISION recorded (no audit, no event in prod wiring app.ts:138).

gaps: No enforcement of trust_status anywhere outside the registry: revoked/blocked devices are never denied (backend or desktop).
No proof-of-possession for deviceId; identity is a client-minted UUID broadcast to every org member via GET /devices and every sync body.

No ownership binding on re-register/heartbeat: member X can overwrite member Y's device row metadata in the same org (PG keeps Y's user_id; in-memory reassigns to X) — repo divergence plus missing check.
No PENDING/approval or EXPIRED state; registration = trusted by default (contradicts NP-OS-DEVICE-REGISTRY-SPEC §8).
'blocked' state has no setter (dead enum value).
Heartbeat endpoint exists but is never called by the desktop; last_seen only moves on Settings-pane visits.
Revocation reaches the device only if the user opens Settings -> Trusted Devices; no push, no timer, no sync consult.
Renderer-asserted trust over a PUBLIC IPC channel; main cannot distinguish a genuine backend answer from a renderer claim.
Backend self-service own-device revoke is absent (owner/admin only), so the desktop's member self-service branch ends in 403.
Bridge permission 'org:manage' on DevicesRegister blocks self-registration for non-admin local principals; GATE10 text says self-register is membership-only.
No HTTP router tests, no integration tests, no UI tests for the devices surface; repository.ts:3-4 claims integration coverage that does not exist.
No audit record and (in production wiring) no domain event for device.registered / revoked / removed.
installations/installation_keys enrolment schema referenced by NP-DEVICE-IDENTITY-GAP-005 is absent from this repo; DEVICE_ID = NOT_ESTABLISHED stands in substance (id exists, identity does not).
No rate limit or per-plan cap on device registration.

gate_assessments.reason: Mechanism exists and is unit-verified (POST /devices, membership-gated, upsert preserves trust/registeredAt; service.test.ts 7/7 MEASURED). Not measured at HTTP or integration level; registration auto-trusts with no approval, no ownership binding, no audit, no limits — whether 'registered == trusted' is acceptable is a human/product decision (GAP-005 step 2).

No enrolment lifecycle: no pending/eligible/activated states, no key enrolment (installation_keys schema absent), no attestation, and revocation does not fail closed on any surface. Evidence: types.ts:11, repository.ts:49, service.ts:63-76, sync/router.ts:44-58, deviceRuntimeState.ts:18-27.

Device identity is a client-minted bearer UUID (liveSyncInstance.ts:84) with no key material, no proof of possession, no server-side generation, no runtime id, not bound to the session token (jwt.ts:32). Spec NP-OS-DEVICE-REGISTRY-SPEC non-conformant; GAP-005 'DEVICE_ID = NOT_ESTABLISHED' remains substantively true.
